P1.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter notes exist to read back, so P1a is N/A. The frame was two-part, not four: 'I just want to get a good idea of where you're at, you know, really build out what it is that you want to accomplish. And if there's alignment, we can talk about the coaching with Trevor.' No 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement was volunteered rather than asked for — the prospect said 'Sounds good' but the rep never asked 'Does that work?'. Open question ran cleanly: 'What was it that you were hoping we could potentially help you out with, man?'

P2.evidence: Only training week and nutrition were asked: 'What does your workouts look like? Like how many days a week are training?' and 'What's your nutrition like? What kind of stuff are you eating?'. Age ('I'm 43 years old'), weight ('I'm about 230 right now'), body fat ('I'm-22% body fat') and occupation ('I'm a massage therapist too') were all volunteered unprompted — no credit. Height, health conditions, injuries, sleep and daytime energy were never raised at all, and the wrist trauma surfaced only because the prospect brought it up.

P3.evidence: The surface goal question was posed as a timeline question rather than a change question: 'Alright, three months down the line, where do you want to be at?'. The bridge to deeper motivation ran well: 'it sounds like you've had a shift in perspective almost... what was that for you that caused that?', which produced the trauma-work and longevity material. But the rep never asked what moving better would actually do for him, never asked who else it impacts, and never drove through to family, legacy or identity even though the prospect handed him the longevity thread ('I got clients in their 80s that are still skiing and climbing mountains'). The reflect-back was a personality mirror rather than the scripted reframe: 'You strike me as... I'm just here to be the best that I can possibly be.'

P4.evidence: Ran as a single compound question scoped only to fat loss: 'When it comes to melting the fat off, what do you feel like has held you back? Like, what have you tried, and why has that not worked, do you think?' The prospect answered on calories and fat intake. The rep then closed it out with 'Probably. Yeah, probably. Do you fast at all?' and never pushed to a structural root cause — no 'one thing getting in the way', no naming of the gap, and never the 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' move, which was the single most available lever on a self-directed prospect.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The rep never asked what the next two years look like if nothing changes, never tested willingness to settle, and never asked for a line in the sand. Instead he closed discovery with praise: 'I think you've shown up very well on this call, firstly. I want to kind of congratulate you on that side of it.'

P6.evidence: No belief question and no all-in question. The only gate before presenting was a soft self-select: 'If you feel like you're ready, I can kind of walk you through what it looks like, the coaching.' The prospect never gave a verbal yes to the outcome, so the offer was presented into an untested commitment — which is exactly where it failed four minutes later.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. After the price objection the rep moved to demo the self-guided product and then accepted the think-about-it, so payment, the Trevor onboarding call, the agreement email and the welcome/Skool steps were never reached.

objection_plays.detail: Clear money trigger at 00:19:12 — 'the 4K, I'm not going to go for that right now'. None of the play ran. No isolation ('finances aside — nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), no 'you're in a HOW place' reframe, no permission question about an honest financial conversation, and none of the six financial-picture questions. The rep's entire response was 'Yeah, I appreciate it. I can show it to you if you like' and a screen share of the cheapest product. Payment plans were never mentioned even though the prospect's stated blocker was a lump sum, not affordability in principle.

Explicit think-about-it at 00:25:00 — 'I got a bit to think about'. No move from the play ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The rep answered 'Yeah, cool, man. Well, just let me know' and handed control of the follow-up to the prospect.

Script gap — 'a cheaper alternative that already works for me', in its purest form. The prospect is self-coaching from free online content with real results (~30 lb lost), is actively evaluating four competing programmes, and is anchored to Primal's own $200/month self-guided tier. There is no scripted play for defending the coaching price against a functioning low-cost substitute, and here the substitute was sold by the rep himself. Same gap already logged against the Badrane Hriouch call.

Script gap — reduced-scope buyer. The prospect wants form critique on a mixed modality set (kettlebell, macebell, sandbag, rings) rather than a full coaching relationship. With no scripted path the rep improvised a price ladder downward, quoting 3 months / $4,000, 6 months / $6,000 and 1 month / $1,200, none of which is the sanctioned offer.

notes: This ran as a product demo, not a sales call: discovery covered training and diet only, and the two phases that create buying pressure — consequence frame and commitment check — were skipped entirely, so the price landed with nothing behind it. Coach the sequence hard: no numbers before a verbal yes, and never volunteer the cheapest tier before the objection has been isolated.
